datasets.title: Preliminary Satellite Derived Flood Evolution Assessment, Islamic Republic of Pakistan-19 October 2022
datasets.description: UNOSAT code FL20220808PAK, GDACS Id: 1101522 Status: Overall decrease of flood waters observed Further action(s): continue monitoring Summary of findings; Evolution of Cumulative Flood Waters over I.R. of Pakistan (03-09 October 2022 Vs 11-17 October 2022): Between 11 and 17 October 2022 approximately 11 million people remain potentially exposed or living close to flooded areas; Based on satellite observations between 03 and 09 October 2022 and compared with observations between 11 and 17 October 2022, the overall flood water extent appears to continue to decrease with approximately 200 km² in Balochistan, ~Punjab 100 km² and ~2,700 km² in Sindh.. [Source: This metadata record was automatically extracted from the Humanitarian Data Exchange (HDX); Original dataset: https://data.humdata.org/dataset/preliminary-satellite-derived-flood-evolution-assessment-islamic-republic-of-pakistan-19-o]
datasets.details: This is a preliminary assessment and has not yet been validated in the field. It is important to consider the characteristics of the source imagery used in the analyses when interpreting results. For damage assessments it should be noted that only significant damage to the structural integrity of the buildings analyzed can be seen in imagery, while minor damage such as cracks or holes may not be visible at all. For flood extractions using radar data it is important to note that urban areas and highly vegetated areas may mask the flood signature and result in underestimation of flood waters. Users with specific questions or concerns should contact unosat@unitar.org to seek clarification.

lineage.description: UNOSAT analysts compared satellite imagery acquired 03-09 October 2022 with imagery from 11-17 October 2022 to detect changes in flood water extent across Pakistan. Flood polygons were delineated through visual interpretation and change detection analysis, with areas calculated in hectares and square meters. The dataset tracks cumulative flood water evolution over time to support emergency response monitoring.

sources.name: UN Operational Satellite Applications Programme (UNOSAT)
sources.description: Multi-temporal satellite imagery analysis using optical sensors to detect and map flood water extent through change detection between pre- and post-event observations
